dentists.heading: Choosing a dentist in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Alpharetta and the rest of North Fulton have a wide choice of general and family dental practices, so the real decision is usually about fit rather than availability. Start with the basics for your household: hours that work around school and commute schedules, a team that is comfortable with young children or anxious adults, and whether the office handles crowns, root canals and implants in house or refers them out. Confirm network status with your insurer directly, because carrier directories and practice websites are not always current.

Dentists and dental hygienists in Georgia are licensed by the Georgia Board of Dentistry. Its online license verification shows the license number, status, issue and expiration dates, and any public disciplinary actions, and you can print the result for your records. Checking takes a minute and is worth doing before you commit to a new office. At the first visit, ask for a written treatment plan with estimated insurance coverage before any work begins, how the office handles a cracked tooth or swelling after hours, and whether recent X-rays can be sent over from your previous dentist so they are not repeated.

Families with children starting school should plan ahead. Fulton County Schools asks for a Georgia ear, eye, dental and nutrition certificate (DPH Form 3300) the first time a child enrolls, so it helps to schedule a checkup well before registration deadlines. Be cautious of an office that presents a long list of urgent treatments at a first cleaning without explaining the reason for each, or that pushes you to sign a financing agreement the same day. Asking for a second opinion on major work is normal, and a good practice will not object.

faqs.q: How do I check if a dentist is licensed in Georgia?
faqs.a: Use the license verification tool on the Georgia Board of Dentistry website. It lists the dentist's license status, expiration date and any public disciplinary actions.

faqs.q: Do Georgia schools require a dental screening?
faqs.a: Yes. Fulton County Schools requires a Georgia ear, eye, dental and nutrition certificate (DPH Form 3300) the first time a child enrolls, and Georgia's Pre-K Program asks for the same certificate within 90 days of entry.

veterinarians.heading: Finding a veterinarian in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Pet owners in Alpharetta can choose from general practice clinics, practices focused on cats or exotic animals, and larger hospitals with surgery and overnight care. Think about what your pet will need over the next several years, not just the next visit. A young dog that spends time on the Big Creek Greenway or at a boarding facility needs different care than an older indoor cat. Ask whether the clinic sees your type of animal routinely, whether one doctor will follow your pet over time, and where the clinic sends patients for after hours emergencies.

Veterinarians in Georgia are licensed by the Georgia State Board of Veterinary Medicine, which is part of the Secretary of State's Professional Licensing Boards. You can confirm a license through the Secretary of State's online license verification tool. Georgia law requires dogs and cats to be vaccinated against rabies under rules set by county boards of health, and the vaccine must be given by a licensed veterinarian, so keep the certificate and tag information handy for boarding, grooming and travel. The warm, humid climate in North Georgia also means fleas, ticks and mosquitoes are active for much of the year, so ask the clinic what year round parasite prevention it recommends for your pet.

When you visit a clinic for the first time, notice whether exam rooms are clean, whether staff explain what they are doing, and whether you receive a written estimate before procedures such as dental cleanings or surgery. Ask how test results are shared and how quickly the clinic returns calls. Red flags include pressure to approve treatment without an explanation, reluctance to share medical records, or no clear plan for emergencies. Routine wellness visits can often be booked within a week or two, while specialty and surgical appointments may take longer.

faqs.q: Is rabies vaccination required for pets in Georgia?
faqs.a: Yes. Georgia law directs county boards of health to require rabies vaccination for dogs and cats, and the vaccine must be given by a licensed veterinarian.

faqs.q: How can I verify a veterinarian's license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Search the veterinarian's name in the Georgia Secretary of State's online license verification tool, which covers the State Board of Veterinary Medicine.

gyms.heading: Choosing a gym or fitness studio in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Alpharetta has everything from large membership gyms to small boutique studios for cycling, yoga, Pilates, boxing and strength training. The best choice is usually the one you will actually use, so start with location and class times. A studio near Avalon or downtown may be easy on a weekday evening but harder on a Saturday, while a gym near your office or your child's school can make early morning workouts realistic. Most places offer a trial class or a short guest pass, and it is worth trying a session at the time of day you plan to go.

Read the membership agreement before you sign. Look for the cancellation policy, how much notice is required, whether there is an annual fee, and whether you can freeze the membership for travel or an injury. Ask whether you can cancel online or by email, or whether you must appear in person or send a letter. For personal training, ask about the trainer's certification and experience with people at your level, and whether sessions expire if you do not use them within a set time. A clear written answer to each question is a good sign.

Summers in North Fulton are hot and humid, which pushes many outdoor runners and cyclists indoors from late spring into early fall, and classes can fill quickly during that stretch and again in January. If you prefer to train outside, the Big Creek Greenway offers a long paved path, and some studios run outdoor sessions in cooler months. Red flags include high pressure sales tactics, reluctance to show you the contract before you pay, locker rooms or equipment that are not kept clean, and staff who cannot explain how to cancel.

faqs.q: What should I check in a gym contract before signing?
faqs.a: Look for the cancellation terms, required notice, annual or enrollment fees, freeze options and how long any prepaid training sessions remain valid. Ask for a copy of the contract before you pay.

faqs.q: Can I try a gym or studio in Alpharetta before joining?
faqs.a: Many gyms and studios offer a free or reduced trial class or a short guest pass. Ask before you visit, and try it at the time of day you plan to work out.

nail-salons.heading: Choosing a nail salon in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Nail salons in Alpharetta range from quick walk in shops in neighborhood shopping centers to appointment based studios that focus on gel, dip powder, structured manicures or nail art. Decide what you want before you book. If you need a reliable weekly manicure, convenience and short wait times matter most. If you want detailed art or a natural nail repair, look at recent photos of the technician's own work and book with that person directly. Weekends and the weeks before holidays, proms and graduations are busiest, so book ahead during those times.

In Georgia, nail technicians and salons are both licensed by the State Board of Cosmetology and Barbers, which is part of the Secretary of State's Professional Licensing Boards. The board requires salon licenses and individual licenses to be posted inside the salon, and salons are subject to random inspections. Look for those licenses on the wall when you walk in, and you can confirm any license through the Secretary of State's online license verification tool. If a technician will not tell you their name or you cannot find a posted license, consider going elsewhere.

Cleanliness is the most important thing to watch. Tools should come from a sealed pouch or be clearly cleaned between clients, files and buffers should be new or used only on you, and pedicure tubs should be cleaned and drained between customers. Ask how the salon cleans its foot spas. It is reasonable to decline a service such as aggressive cuticle cutting or callus shaving if it makes you uncomfortable. Signs of a problem include strong lingering fumes with poor ventilation, reused emery boards, dirty towels, and pain or redness after a visit that does not fade.

faqs.q: Do nail technicians need a license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Yes. Nail technicians and the salons they work in are licensed by the Georgia State Board of Cosmetology and Barbers, and both licenses must be posted in the salon.

faqs.q: Are nail salons inspected in Georgia?
faqs.a: Yes. The State Board of Cosmetology and Barbers says all salons are subject to random inspections, and citations can be issued for violations.

real-estate-agents.heading: Hiring a real estate agent in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Alpharetta's housing market includes established swim and tennis subdivisions, newer townhome communities, golf course neighborhoods, condos near Avalon and downtown, and larger lots toward the Milton line. An agent who regularly works in your target area will know which neighborhoods have active homeowners associations, how resale values have moved, and what buyers there expect. Ask each candidate how many transactions they closed in Alpharetta or nearby North Fulton communities over the past year, and whether they mostly represent buyers or sellers.

Real estate agents and brokers in Georgia are licensed by the Georgia Real Estate Commission, and the commission offers an online licensee search where you can confirm that an agent's license is active. Before you sign any agreement, read how long it lasts, how the agent is paid, and what happens if you want to end it early. For buyers, ask how the agent will help you review HOA covenants, fees and rental restrictions, since these vary widely between Alpharetta neighborhoods. School attendance zones are set by Fulton County Schools, so confirm any zoning claim with the district rather than relying on a listing.

A good agent will explain local pricing using recent comparable sales rather than promises, and will be clear about who they represent in the transaction. Ask how they handle inspections, appraisal gaps and negotiations over repairs, and which inspectors, lenders and closing attorneys they work with, along with whether you are free to choose your own. Red flags include pressure to sign quickly, vague answers about fees, or an agent who discourages you from getting a home inspection. Interviewing two or three agents before choosing is common and expected.

faqs.q: How do I check a real estate agent's license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Use the licensee search offered by the Georgia Real Estate Commission, where you can confirm that an agent holds an active license.

faqs.q: How do I confirm which school a home is zoned for in Alpharetta?
faqs.a: Check the address with Fulton County Schools directly, since attendance zones are set by the district and can change. Do not rely only on a listing description.

kids-activities.heading: Choosing kids activities and classes in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Alpharetta families can choose from private studios for dance, martial arts, music, swim, gymnastics and STEM, along with youth sports leagues and city programs. The City of Alpharetta's Recreation, Parks and Culture department publishes Recreation and Arts Guides listing its classes and programs, and it runs summer camps and programs such as iCan Bike. Start by matching the activity to your child's age and temperament, then look at schedule and drive time. A class that sounds perfect can become a burden if it means crossing Highway 9 or GA 400 at rush hour twice a week.

Before you register, ask about instructor experience and training, how staff are screened, the adult to child ratio, and how the program handles injuries, allergies and pickup. Ask whether parents can watch a class or attend a trial session, and what the refund or make up policy is if your child is sick or decides the activity is not a fit. For full day camps and care, ask whether the program is licensed by Georgia's Department of Early Care and Learning or operates under an exemption, and what that means for supervision and staffing.

Popular summer camps and fall programs in North Fulton often fill early, so watch for registration dates in late winter and late summer. Hot, humid summers make shade, water breaks and indoor backup plans important for outdoor camps and sports. Red flags include instructors who will not let parents observe, unclear emergency procedures, no written policies, or pressure to commit to a long contract before a trial. A good program will be happy to answer questions and introduce you to the instructor.

faqs.q: Does the City of Alpharetta offer kids classes and camps?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's Recreation, Parks and Culture department offers youth programs and summer camps, which are listed in its Recreation and Arts Guides on the city website.

faqs.q: What should I ask a kids activity program before signing up?
faqs.a: Ask about instructor screening and training, class size, how injuries and allergies are handled, the pickup policy and the refund or make up policy.

electricians.heading: Hiring an electrician in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Alpharetta homeowners often call electricians to add circuits for home offices, EV chargers, kitchen remodels, generators or finished basements. Summer thunderstorms in North Georgia also bring power surges and outages, which lead to questions about surge protection and standby generators. Before calling, write down what you want done, the age of the house, and the size of your electrical panel if you know it, so you can get comparable quotes.

Electrical contractors in Georgia are licensed by the Division of Electrical Contractors of the State Construction Industry Licensing Board, part of the Secretary of State's office. There are two statewide contractor classes. A Class I license is restricted to single phase work that does not exceed 200 amperes at the service, which covers most single family homes, while a Class II license is unrestricted. Ask for the license number and check it through the Secretary of State's online license verification tool. For larger jobs such as panel upgrades, new circuits or generator hookups, ask who will pull the City of Alpharetta permit and schedule inspections, and make sure that responsibility is written into the agreement.

Get written estimates from at least two contractors that describe the work, materials, permit responsibility and warranty. Ask about proof of liability insurance and whether the person doing the work is an employee or a subcontractor. Red flags include an electrician who suggests skipping the permit, asks for most of the payment up front, cannot provide a license number, or diagnoses a major problem without testing. Small service calls can often be scheduled within days, while panel upgrades and generator installs may take longer because of permits, equipment and utility coordination.

faqs.q: Do electricians need a license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Yes. Electrical contractors are licensed by the Division of Electrical Contractors of the State Construction Industry Licensing Board. A Class I license covers single phase work up to 200 amps at the service, and a Class II license is unrestricted.

faqs.q: How do I look up an electrician's license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Search the contractor's name or license number in the Georgia Secretary of State's online license verification tool.

roofers.heading: Hiring a roofer in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Roofs in Alpharetta take a beating from summer heat and humidity, heavy thunderstorms, occasional hail and wind, and the odd winter ice storm. In neighborhoods built around the same time, entire streets can reach replacement age together, and storms can bring a wave of door to door contractors. If you live in a community with a homeowners association, check the covenants before you choose shingles, since many HOAs require approval for roof color or material.

Georgia does not issue a separate license for roofing. The Secretary of State's contractor licensing board lists shingle, sheet metal and flat roofing as specialty trades, so a roofer working only within that specialty is not required to hold a state residential or general contractor license. That makes your own checks more important. Ask for a physical business address, proof of liability and workers compensation insurance, and local references from recent jobs. Ask who will pull any required City of Alpharetta permit and arrange inspections, and get the manufacturer's warranty and the contractor's workmanship warranty in writing.

After a hail or wind storm, document the damage with photos and contact your insurance company before signing anything with a contractor. Be wary of anyone who shows up uninvited, offers to waive your deductible, asks you to sign a contract that gives them control of your insurance claim, or wants a large payment before materials are delivered. A good written estimate lists the shingle brand and line, underlayment, ventilation, flashing and how rotted decking will be handled. Replacement work after a major storm can take weeks to schedule, while small repairs are usually quicker.

faqs.q: Do roofers need a license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Georgia has no roofing specific license. The state contractor board treats shingle, metal and flat roofing as specialty trades, so check insurance, references and a written warranty instead.

faqs.q: Does my HOA need to approve a new roof in Alpharetta?
faqs.a: Many HOAs require approval for roof color or material. Check your community's covenants and submit any required request before work starts.

tree-service.heading: Hiring a tree service in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Alpharetta's mature hardwoods and tall pines are part of what makes its neighborhoods appealing, but they also bring risk during summer thunderstorms, high winds and winter ice storms. Homeowners usually call a tree service for three reasons: storm damage, a dead or declining tree near the house, or pruning to clear roofs, driveways and power lines. Before calling, note the species if you know it, the tree's size and location, and anything nearby such as fences, decks or utility lines.

The City of Alpharetta requires a tree removal permit for most removals in the city, and on single family residential property the permit must be approved before removing any tree that is alive. The City Arborist reviews removal applications for private property, and residents can send questions through the city's Ask the Arborist form. The city also runs an Authorized Tree Removal Contractor Program for companies that have completed a training class taught by the City Arborist, which can speed up approval for certain removals. Ask any company you are considering whether it participates and who will handle the permit. Emergency and storm removals are handled case by case.

Ask each company for proof of liability and workers compensation insurance, since tree work is dangerous and injuries on your property are a real concern. A written estimate should say whether stump grinding, cleanup and hauling are included. Ask whether an arborist will assess the tree before recommending removal. Red flags include topping a healthy tree, using climbing spikes on trees that are only being pruned, door to door offers right after a storm, and requests for full payment before work begins.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to remove a tree in Alpharetta?
faqs.a: Usually yes. The City of Alpharetta requires a tree removal permit for most removals, and on single family residential property the permit must be approved before a living tree is removed.

faqs.q: What is Alpharetta's Authorized Tree Removal Contractor Program?
faqs.a: It is a city program for tree contractors who have completed a training class taught by the City Arborist, which lets them get faster approval for certain removals.

pest-control.heading: Hiring a pest control company in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: North Fulton's warm, humid climate keeps pests active much of the year. Homeowners commonly deal with ants, roaches, spiders, mosquitoes, rodents in the colder months, and termites, which are a concern for wood framed houses on crawl spaces and slabs alike. Before you call, note what you are seeing, where and when, and whether you have pets or small children, since that affects which treatments make sense. Ask whether a company is quoting a one time service or a recurring plan, and what is included in each visit.

Structural pest control in Georgia is regulated by the Georgia Department of Agriculture. Every pest control company must hold a company license and designate a Certified Operator for each category it works in, such as household pests or wood destroying organisms like termites. Employees who sell or perform pest control must be registered by the company, and company vehicles must be marked with the company name. The department has warned consumers about unlicensed door to door pest control sales and accepts reports of unlicensed operators, so ask for the company license number and check it before you agree to anything.

For termites, ask whether the company offers a written termite bond, what it covers, whether it is a retreat only or a repair and retreat agreement, and how often inspections occur. A termite letter may also be needed when you sell a home. Get the treatment plan in writing, including the products to be used and any precautions for pets. Red flags include pressure to sign up the same day, a salesperson who will not leave written information, and anyone who cannot name the licensed company they work for.

faqs.q: Do pest control companies need a license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Yes. The Georgia Department of Agriculture licenses structural pest control companies, and each company must have a Certified Operator for every category of work it performs.

faqs.q: How do I report an unlicensed pest control company in Georgia?
faqs.a: The Georgia Department of Agriculture accepts reports of unlicensed structural pest control operators through its website.

landscaping.heading: Hiring a landscaping or lawn care company in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Alpharetta lawns deal with red clay soil, hot humid summers, heavy spring pollen and occasional drought. Many yards are planted with warm season grasses such as Bermuda or zoysia, while shady lots under mature trees often struggle to keep any grass at all. Before getting quotes, decide whether you need weekly mowing, seasonal fertilization and weed control, or design and installation work such as new beds, drainage or hardscaping. If you live in an HOA community, check whether plant choices, fences or new features need approval.

Any business that applies pesticides, including weed control and insect treatments, to someone else's property for a fee must hold a pesticide contractor license from the Georgia Department of Agriculture, and lawn care companies are specifically included. Ask for the license if a company offers chemical treatments. Georgia's statewide outdoor watering rules also matter for new installs. Outside of drought restrictions, irrigation of lawns and plants is allowed daily between 4 p.m. and 10 a.m., while new plantings are exempt during installation and for 30 days after, and drip irrigation, soaker hoses and hand watering are exempt at any time. A good contractor will set irrigation timers within those rules.

Get written proposals that spell out the schedule, what each visit includes, who supplies plants and mulch, and any guarantee on new plants. Ask whether the crew is employed by the company or subcontracted, and confirm liability insurance. Red flags include no written agreement, pressure to prepay a full season, and treatments applied without notice. Spring and fall are the busiest seasons in North Fulton, so book installation projects early.

faqs.q: Do lawn care companies need a license in Georgia?
faqs.a: A company that applies pesticides, including weed control, to other people's property for a fee needs a pesticide contractor license from the Georgia Department of Agriculture.

faqs.q: What are the watering rules in Alpharetta?
faqs.a: Under Georgia's non-drought outdoor water use rules, landscape irrigation is allowed daily between 4 p.m. and 10 a.m. New plantings for 30 days, drip irrigation and hand watering are exempt.

orthodontists.heading: Choosing an orthodontist in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Orthodontic care usually lasts a year or more, so choosing an office in Alpharetta often comes down to convenience as much as anything else. Many visits are short adjustment appointments, and for students that means finding after school or early morning slots near home or school. The American Association of Orthodontists recommends that children have a first check up with an orthodontist by age 7. That visit does not mean treatment will start right away. Often the orthodontist simply monitors growth and recommends a later start.

Orthodontists in Georgia are dentists, and their licenses are issued by the Georgia Board of Dentistry. The board's online license verification shows the license status, expiration date and any public disciplinary actions. At a consultation, ask about the treatment options for your case, such as traditional braces or clear aligners, the expected length of treatment, how often visits will be, and what happens if treatment takes longer than planned. Ask what is included in the quoted fee, including retainers, emergency visits for broken brackets and follow up after the braces come off.

Getting two consultations is common, so compare treatment plans as well as personalities. Ask how the office communicates with your general dentist and how it handles missed appointments during busy school seasons. Red flags include pressure to start treatment the same day, vague answers about what is included, or a plan that does not explain why early treatment is needed for a young child. Keep up regular cleanings with your family dentist throughout treatment.

faqs.q: What age should a child first see an orthodontist?
faqs.a: The American Association of Orthodontists recommends a first orthodontic check up by age 7. Treatment may not begin then, but the orthodontist can monitor growth and spot issues early.

faqs.q: How do I verify an orthodontist's license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Orthodontists are licensed dentists, so you can check their license through the Georgia Board of Dentistry's online license verification.

pediatricians.heading: Choosing a pediatrician in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Many Alpharetta parents start looking for a pediatrician during pregnancy, since newborns are usually seen within days of coming home. Pediatric practices in North Fulton range from small offices with a few doctors to large groups with several locations and extended hours. Decide what matters most to your family: a doctor you will see at nearly every visit, same day sick appointments, weekend hours, or a location close to home or daycare. Confirm the practice is in network with your insurance and is accepting new patients before you schedule a meet and greet.

Pediatricians in Georgia are licensed by the Georgia Composite Medical Board, which offers an online tool to verify a physician's license and see whether the board has issued any public orders. At a first visit, ask how the practice handles after hours calls, which hospital it is affiliated with, how quickly sick children are seen, and whether nurse practitioners or physician assistants see patients. Ask how the office communicates test results and refill requests, whether through a patient portal, phone or text.

School and child care paperwork is a practical reason to have a pediatrician you can reach. Fulton County Schools requires a Georgia Certificate of Immunization (DPH Form 3231) for every student, plus an ear, eye, dental and nutrition certificate (DPH Form 3300) the first time a child enrolls, and Georgia's Pre-K Program asks for these forms soon after a child starts. Ask how long the office takes to complete forms. Spring pollen season and the winter cold and flu months are the busiest times for sick visits, so learn the practice's same day scheduling process early.

faqs.q: What forms does my child need for school in Georgia?
faqs.a: Fulton County Schools requires a Georgia Certificate of Immunization (DPH Form 3231) and, the first time a child enrolls, an ear, eye, dental and nutrition certificate (DPH Form 3300). Your pediatrician can complete both.

faqs.q: How do I check a pediatrician's license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Use the Georgia Composite Medical Board's online license verification, which shows the physician's license status and any public board orders.

urgent-care.heading: Using an urgent care clinic in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Urgent care clinics in Alpharetta fill the gap between your regular doctor and the emergency room. They are commonly used for minor illnesses and injuries such as sore throats, ear infections, minor cuts, sprains and rashes, especially in the evening or on weekends when a primary care office is closed. Spring pollen season and the winter cold and flu months tend to be the busiest times. Some clinics treat children of all ages while others have age limits, so check before you go if you are bringing a young child.

Know when urgent care is not the right place. Chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of stroke, severe bleeding, serious head injuries or a very sick infant call for 911 or an emergency department. A nearby hospital emergency department is Wellstar North Fulton Medical Center on Hospital Boulevard in Roswell, which is a verified Level II trauma center. If you are unsure, call your doctor's nurse line or ask the urgent care staff by phone before driving over.

Before you need one, find out which clinics near home and work accept your insurance and whether they offer online check in to reduce waiting. Check whether the clinic has on site X-ray and lab testing, since that can save a second trip. Physicians working at urgent care centers are licensed by the Georgia Composite Medical Board, and you can look them up online. After a visit, ask the clinic to send records to your primary care doctor so your file stays complete.

faqs.q: When should I go to the ER instead of urgent care?
faqs.a: Call 911 or go to an emergency department for chest pain, trouble breathing, stroke symptoms, severe bleeding or serious injuries. Urgent care is meant for minor illnesses and injuries.

faqs.q: Where is a hospital emergency room near Alpharetta?
faqs.a: Wellstar North Fulton Medical Center at 3000 Hospital Boulevard in Roswell has an emergency department and is a Level II trauma center.

physical-therapy.heading: Choosing a physical therapist in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Alpharetta residents see physical therapists for back and neck pain, sports injuries, recovery after joint replacement or surgery, balance problems and work related strain. Clinics differ in focus. Some concentrate on orthopedic and sports care, while others specialize in pelvic health, vestibular problems, pediatrics or neurological conditions. Ask whether the therapist you will see has experience with your specific problem, and whether you will work with the same therapist at each visit or rotate between staff.

Physical therapists in Georgia are licensed by the Georgia State Board of Physical Therapy, part of the Secretary of State's Professional Licensing Boards, and you can confirm a license through the Secretary of State's online verification tool. Georgia allows patients to start physical therapy without a physician referral in many cases, but under state law the therapist must obtain a referral from a physician or dentist after 21 days or eight visits, with some exceptions. Many insurance plans also have their own referral and authorization rules, so call your insurer before the first appointment to avoid surprise bills.

At the first visit, a good therapist will evaluate you, explain what they found, and set goals and an expected number of visits. Ask how much of each session is one on one time with a licensed therapist, how home exercises will be taught and progressed, and how progress will be measured. Red flags include sessions that are mostly unsupervised, no written plan, or a recommendation for open ended visits without clear goals. Early morning and evening appointments fill quickly, so ask about scheduling before you commit.

faqs.q: Do I need a referral to see a physical therapist in Georgia?
faqs.a: Not always. Georgia allows direct access to physical therapy, but the therapist must get a physician or dentist referral after 21 days or eight visits, with some exceptions, and your insurer may have its own rules.

faqs.q: How do I verify a physical therapist's license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Search for the therapist in the Georgia Secretary of State's online license verification tool, which covers the State Board of Physical Therapy.

chiropractors.heading: Choosing a chiropractor in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: People in Alpharetta often see chiropractors for low back pain, neck pain, headaches and stiffness from long commutes or desk work. Practices vary a great deal. Some focus on spinal adjustments, while others combine adjustments with exercise, soft tissue work or coordination with physical therapists and medical doctors. Before booking, decide what you want from care and look for a practice whose approach matches. If you have had a recent injury, a car accident, numbness or weakness, it is wise to see a medical doctor as well.

Chiropractors in Georgia are licensed by the Georgia Board of Chiropractic Examiners, part of the Secretary of State's Professional Licensing Boards. The board reviews applications, licenses qualified chiropractors and investigates complaints, and it can take disciplinary action when warranted. You can confirm a chiropractor's license through the Secretary of State's online license verification tool. Also ask your insurance company whether chiropractic care is covered, whether a referral is needed, and how many visits a year the plan allows.

At the first visit, a chiropractor should take a history, do an exam, explain the findings and describe a treatment plan with goals and a time frame. Ask how progress will be measured and when you should expect improvement. Red flags include pressure to prepay for a long series of visits, a plan that does not change as you improve, routine X-rays for everyone without a clear reason, and claims that adjustments can cure unrelated illnesses. You should feel free to stop care or seek another opinion at any point.

faqs.q: Do chiropractors need a license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Yes. Chiropractors are licensed by the Georgia Board of Chiropractic Examiners, which also investigates complaints about licensees.

faqs.q: Should I prepay for a package of chiropractic visits?
faqs.a: Be cautious with large prepaid packages. A sound treatment plan has clear goals and is adjusted as you improve, and you should be able to stop care at any time.

counseling.heading: Finding a counselor or therapist in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Counselors and therapists in Alpharetta work with individuals, couples, families and children on concerns such as anxiety, depression, grief, relationship stress, parenting and life transitions. Many offer both in person sessions and telehealth, which can make it easier to fit appointments around work and school. Start by thinking about what you want help with and any preferences you have, such as a therapist's gender, faith background or experience with teenagers. Most therapists offer a brief phone call before the first session to see whether you are a good fit.

Several types of licensed professionals provide therapy in Georgia. Professional counselors, clinical social workers and marriage and family therapists are licensed by the Georgia Composite Board of Professional Counselors, Social Workers and Marriage and Family Therapists, and psychologists are licensed by the Georgia State Board of Examiners of Psychologists. Both boards are part of the Secretary of State's Professional Licensing Boards, and you can check a license through the Secretary of State's online verification tool. Some newer clinicians hold associate level licenses and practice under supervision, so ask who supervises them.

Before starting, ask whether the therapist accepts your insurance or provides paperwork for out of network reimbursement, how cancellations are handled, and how long the wait is for a regular weekly time. Ask what approaches they use and how you will know whether therapy is working. Fit matters, and it is fine to try someone else if the relationship does not feel right after a few sessions. If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, or call 911.

faqs.q: How do I check if a therapist is licensed in Georgia?
faqs.a: Search the therapist's name in the Georgia Secretary of State's online license verification tool, which covers licensed professional counselors, clinical social workers, marriage and family therapists and psychologists.

faqs.q: What is the difference between an LPC, LCSW and LMFT?
faqs.a: All three are licensed therapists in Georgia under the same composite board. LPCs are professional counselors, LCSWs are clinical social workers and LMFTs are marriage and family therapists, and each has its own training path.

accountants.heading: Hiring a CPA or accountant in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Alpharetta is home to many small businesses, technology professionals and households with more complex finances, so local accounting firms cover a wide range of work: individual tax returns, bookkeeping and payroll for small companies, business tax filings, financial statement work and help with IRS or Georgia Department of Revenue notices. Start by deciding what you need. A household with a single W-2 has different needs than a business owner with employees or someone with rental property, stock compensation or income in more than one state.

In Georgia, certified public accountants and CPA firms are licensed by the Georgia State Board of Accountancy. The board's website links to a CPA license search, so you can confirm that someone who uses the CPA title holds an active license. Not everyone who prepares taxes is a CPA, and that is not always a problem for simple returns, but you should know what credentials you are paying for. Ask how long the person has worked with clients like you, who will actually prepare your return, and who reviews it.

Tax season in North Fulton fills up quickly, and some firms stop taking new clients by late winter, so reach out early in the year or in the fall. Ask how the firm will collect documents securely, how it communicates, and what happens if you receive a notice after filing. Get the engagement terms in writing. Red flags include a preparer who will not sign the return, promises of an unusually large refund, fees based on a percentage of your refund, or a request to have your refund deposited into their account.

faqs.q: How do I verify a CPA license in Georgia?
faqs.a: The Georgia State Board of Accountancy website links to a CPA license search where you can confirm an individual's license status.

faqs.q: When should I hire an accountant for tax season?
faqs.a: Reach out in the fall or early in the year. Some firms reach capacity before the spring filing deadline and may stop accepting new clients.

financial-advisors.heading: Choosing a financial advisor in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Alpharetta has a large number of financial advisors, from solo planners to branches of national firms. The title financial advisor is used broadly, so start by learning how a professional is registered and paid. Investment adviser representatives typically have a fiduciary duty when giving investment advice, while brokers sell securities and are held to a different standard of conduct. Some professionals are both. Ask each advisor directly which role they play for you, and ask for their Form CRS, a short disclosure document that explains services, fees and conflicts.

You can check a professional's background for free. FINRA BrokerCheck covers brokers and firms, and the SEC's Investment Adviser Public Disclosure site covers investment advisers, including any disciplinary history. Smaller investment advisers that are not registered with the SEC generally register with the Georgia Secretary of State's Securities Division instead. Look for consistency between what an advisor tells you and what these records show, and take note of any customer complaints or regulatory actions.

In a first meeting, ask how the advisor is compensated, whether through a percentage of assets, flat or hourly fees, commissions or a mix, and what you will pay in total including fund expenses. Ask what services are included, how often you will meet, who holds your assets, and how they handle a market downturn. Red flags include guaranteed returns, pressure to move money quickly, reluctance to put fees in writing, and products you do not understand. This information is general consumer guidance and not financial advice.

faqs.q: How do I check a financial advisor's background?
faqs.a: Search the advisor and firm on FINRA BrokerCheck and the SEC's Investment Adviser Public Disclosure site. Both are free and show registrations and any disciplinary history.

faqs.q: Who regulates financial advisors in Georgia?
faqs.a: Larger investment advisers register with the SEC, while smaller advisers generally register with the Georgia Secretary of State's Securities Division. Brokers are overseen by FINRA.

law-firms.heading: Hiring a lawyer in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Law firms in Alpharetta handle a wide range of matters, including real estate closings, wills and estate planning, business formation and contracts, family law, personal injury, employment issues and traffic or criminal cases in local courts. Start by naming the type of problem you have, since most lawyers concentrate on a few practice areas. A lawyer who regularly handles your kind of matter in Fulton County will know the local courts, procedures and typical timelines.

Every lawyer who practices in Georgia must be a member of the State Bar of Georgia. The State Bar's website offers a member directory where you can check a lawyer's membership, along with a directory for finding lawyers by practice area and information on filing a complaint. The State Bar does not refer clients directly, but local bar associations and approved referral services can help, and families with limited income can look for free civil legal help through georgialegalaid.org.

At a first consultation, ask how much experience the lawyer has with matters like yours, who will handle the day to day work, how and how often they will update you, and what the likely steps and timeline are. Ask how fees are charged, whether hourly, flat fee or contingency, and get the fee agreement in writing before work begins. Red flags include guarantees about the outcome, pressure to sign immediately, or vague answers about billing. This page offers general consumer guidance only and is not legal advice.

faqs.q: How do I check if a lawyer is licensed in Georgia?
faqs.a: Search the State Bar of Georgia's member directory on its website. Lawyers who practice in Georgia must be members of the State Bar.

faqs.q: Can I get free legal help in Alpharetta?
faqs.a: Households with limited income can look for free civil legal services or pro bono help through georgialegalaid.org, which the State Bar of Georgia points the public to.

preschools.heading: Choosing a preschool or daycare in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Alpharetta families can choose from licensed child care centers, church affiliated and private preschools, Montessori programs, family child care homes and Georgia's Pre-K classrooms. Start with logistics: hours that match your work schedule, location relative to home or commute, and whether you need full day care or a part day program. Waiting lists are common for infant rooms and popular programs in North Fulton, so many parents begin touring several months before they need care.

Child care in Georgia is overseen by the Department of Early Care and Learning, also called DECAL or Bright from the Start. Its online provider search lets you find licensed programs and review monitoring visit reports, which is one of the most useful checks you can make. Look for Quality Rated status as well. It is a voluntary rating system, and providers that take part earn one to three stars, with three stars being the highest level. Georgia's Pre-K Program is offered at no cost to families for children who turn four on or before September 1 and live in Georgia. It is available in public schools and private centers, runs about 6.5 hours a day on a school calendar, and each provider sets its own application dates.

When touring, ask about teacher to child ratios, staff training and turnover, the daily schedule, how naps, meals and allergies are handled, and how the program communicates with parents. Watch how teachers talk with children. Red flags include programs that discourage unannounced visits, unclear sick child policies, or a monitoring history with repeated issues. Keep immunization and health forms current, since Pre-K requires Georgia DPH Forms 3231 and 3300 soon after enrollment.

faqs.q: Is Georgia Pre-K free?
faqs.a: Yes. Georgia's Pre-K Program is lottery funded and offered at no cost to families for Georgia children who turn four on or before September 1. Spaces are limited and each provider sets its own application process.

faqs.q: How do I check a daycare's inspection history in Georgia?
faqs.a: Use the provider search on DECAL's website, which shows licensed programs, monitoring visit reports and Quality Rated status.

faqs.q: How old must a child be for kindergarten in Fulton County Schools?
faqs.a: A child must be five years old by September 1 to enroll in kindergarten in Fulton County Schools, with limited exceptions for some students moving from other states.

faqs.q: Do HVAC contractors need a license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Yes. Georgia licenses HVAC contractors as conditioned air contractors through the State Construction Industry Licensing Board. A Class I license is restricted to systems up to 175,000 BTU of heating and 60,000 BTU of cooling, and a Class II license is unrestricted.

faqs.q: How do I check an HVAC contractor's license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Search the contractor's name or license number in the Georgia Secretary of State's online license verification tool.

faqs.q: Do plumbers need a license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Yes. Plumbers are licensed by the State Construction Industry Licensing Board. A Master Plumber Class I license covers single family homes and smaller buildings, and a Class II license is unrestricted.

faqs.q: How can I check a plumber's license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Ask for the license number and search it in the Georgia Secretary of State's online license verification tool.

faqs.q: Do cars in Alpharetta need an emissions test?
faqs.a: Yes, for most gasoline powered passenger vehicles. Fulton County is one of the 13 metro Atlanta counties covered by Georgia's emissions inspection program.

faqs.q: Should I get a written estimate before auto repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask for a written estimate that lists parts and labor, and ask the shop to call you for approval before doing any extra work.

faqs.q: Who can perform laser treatments in Georgia?
faqs.a: Georgia licenses cosmetic laser practitioners through the Georgia Composite Medical Board at two levels, assistant laser practitioner and senior laser practitioner. Ask to see the license of whoever will perform your treatment.

faqs.q: What should I ask at a med spa consultation?
faqs.a: Ask who will perform the treatment and what license they hold, which licensed medical professional oversees the practice, what the risks and recovery look like, and how complications are handled.

hair-salons.heading: Choosing a hair salon in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Alpharetta has everything from one chair studios in salon suite buildings to busy full service salons with a dozen stylists. Before you book, decide what you actually need. A precision cut, a big color change, extensions and keratin treatments all call for different skills, so look for a stylist whose portfolio shows recent work on hair like yours, not just polished photos from a product brand.

Georgia requires every salon to be licensed by the Georgia State Board of Cosmetology and Barbers before it opens, and Board rules say the salon license, or a printout of its online verification, must be posted within fifteen feet of the entrance. Each stylist must also display a current license, and the most recent inspection report has to be posted where customers can see it. In buildings divided into salon suites, licenses should make clear which business each stylist works under. If you cannot spot these documents, ask. A licensed professional will not mind.

For color or chemical services, ask whether the stylist does a consultation and a strand or patch test first, how long the appointment will take, and what the policy is if you are unhappy with the result. Red flags include tools that look unwashed, reused disposable items, and pressure to add services you did not request. Popular stylists in North Fulton often book out weeks ahead of holidays, proms and wedding season, so plan early for big events and confirm the cancellation policy in writing.

faqs.q: Do hair salons need a license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Yes. Salons must be licensed by the Georgia State Board of Cosmetology and Barbers before doing business, and each stylist needs an individual license or permit. Both should be posted in an open area of the salon.

faqs.q: How can I check a salon's inspection record?
faqs.a: Georgia Board rules require salons to post their most recent inspection report in an open area. You can ask to see it if it is not obvious when you walk in.

faqs.q: What should I ask before a major color change?
faqs.a: Ask about a consultation, a strand test, the expected time in the chair, and the salon's policy for corrections. Bring photos of what you want and what you do not want.

barbershops.heading: Finding a good barbershop in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: A good barber learns how your hair grows, how you wear it on an ordinary Tuesday, and how often you come back. In Alpharetta you will find classic walk in shops, appointment only studios and shops inside salon suite buildings, so start by deciding whether you value convenience or a consistent chair with the same barber every visit. Look at recent photos of fades, tapers, beard work and kids' cuts, and pick someone whose everyday work matches the style you want.

Barbershops in Georgia fall under the Georgia State Board of Cosmetology and Barbers. A shop must be licensed before it opens, its license or online verification must be displayed near the entrance, and every barber working there must post a current individual license. Shops also have to post their most recent inspection report and the state's health and sanitation rules. Clean clippers, fresh neck strips, disinfected combs and a tidy station are basic expectations, not extras.

Ask how the shop handles waits, whether online booking holds your spot, and what the policy is for late arrivals or no shows. If you are bringing a child for a first haircut, ask whether a barber is comfortable with young kids and which times are quietest. Weekends and the days before school starts in August tend to fill up fast around North Fulton, so book ahead. If a shop seems to rush every cut or will not answer basic questions, keep looking.

faqs.q: Do barbers need a license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Yes. Barbers are licensed by the Georgia State Board of Cosmetology and Barbers, and Board rules require each barber's current license or online verification to be posted in the shop.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a barbershop and a salon in Georgia?
faqs.a: Both are licensed by the same state board, and many shops hold a single salon or shop license. The real difference is usually the services and style each business focuses on.

faqs.q: How often should I get a fade touched up?
faqs.a: Many people with short fades return every two to three weeks to keep the lines sharp. Ask your barber what interval suits your hair growth.

dermatologists.heading: Choosing a dermatologist in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Dermatology practices in Alpharetta range from large groups with several locations to small offices focused on cosmetic treatments. Start by being clear about why you are going. A skin check, a stubborn rash, acne care and cosmetic procedures are very different visits, and some practices lean heavily toward one type. Ask the office who will actually see you, whether a physician, a physician assistant or a nurse practitioner, and how follow up questions are handled between visits.

Every physician practicing in Georgia must be licensed by the Georgia Composite Medical Board, and the Board's free online lookup shows license status, the date it was first issued, its expiration date and any public Board orders. It is worth a quick search before your first appointment. You can also ask whether the doctor is board certified in dermatology, which reflects specialty training beyond a basic medical license, and whether the practice performs procedures in its own office.

Call your insurance plan or check its directory to confirm the practice is in network, and ask whether you need a referral from a primary care doctor. New patient waits can be long in North Fulton, so ask to be placed on a cancellation list. Be cautious if a practice pushes expensive product packages during a medical visit or will not explain the purpose of a recommended procedure. This guide is general consumer information, so talk with a qualified clinician about any specific skin concern.

faqs.q: How do I check a dermatologist's license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Use the Georgia Composite Medical Board's online licensee search. It shows license status, issue and expiration dates, and any public orders issued by the Board.

faqs.q: Do I need a referral to see a dermatologist?
faqs.a: It depends on your insurance plan. Many HMO style plans require a referral from your primary care doctor, so check with your insurer before booking.

faqs.q: Who might I see at a dermatology appointment?
faqs.a: Many practices use physician assistants and nurse practitioners alongside dermatologists. Ask when booking if you want to see a physician specifically.

eye-doctors.heading: Choosing an eye doctor in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Start by knowing which kind of eye doctor fits your visit. Optometrists handle routine eye exams, glasses and contact lens prescriptions, and many common eye conditions. Ophthalmologists are medical doctors who also perform eye surgery and manage more complex disease. Around Alpharetta you will find optometrists in private practices and inside retail optical stores, while ophthalmology groups usually have dedicated offices and often see patients by referral.

In Georgia, optometrists are licensed through the State Board of Optometry under the Secretary of State, and ophthalmologists, as physicians, are licensed by the Georgia Composite Medical Board, which offers a free online lookup showing license status and any public orders. The optometry board notes that the standard of care for a virtual eye exam is the same as for an in person exam, so ask exactly what an online or kiosk style test includes before relying on it for a prescription.

Vision insurance and medical insurance often work separately, so ask the office which plan will be billed for your visit, especially if you are going for a problem like an infection or floaters rather than a routine exam. Ask whether a contact lens fitting is included or billed separately, and request a copy of your glasses prescription so you can shop around. Back to school season is busy for pediatric exams in North Fulton, so book early in summer. For sudden vision changes, contact a doctor right away rather than waiting for a routine appointment.

faqs.q: What is the difference between an optometrist and an ophthalmologist?
faqs.a: Optometrists provide eye exams, prescriptions and care for many common eye conditions. Ophthalmologists are medical doctors who also perform surgery and treat more complex eye disease.

faqs.q: Can I get a copy of my glasses prescription?
faqs.a: Ask the office for a copy after your exam so you can buy glasses wherever you like. Having it on file also helps if you switch providers.

faqs.q: Are virtual eye exams allowed in Georgia?
faqs.a: The Georgia State Board of Optometry says optometrists can perform virtual eye exams, held to the same standard of care as an in person exam. Ask what testing is included before you book.

primary-care.heading: Finding a primary care doctor in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: A primary care doctor is your long term home base for checkups, preventive screenings, everyday illnesses and referrals to specialists. Alpharetta has a mix of hospital affiliated practices, independent family medicine and internal medicine offices, and concierge style practices. Decide first whether you want one doctor for the whole family, which points to family medicine, or an adult focused internist, and whether the hospital system a practice belongs to matters to you.

Before you book, confirm the practice is in network with your insurance and accepting new patients, since many popular North Fulton offices have long waits for a first visit. Every physician practicing in Georgia must hold a license from the Georgia Composite Medical Board, and the Board's online lookup shows license status, issue and expiration dates and any public orders. A quick search takes a minute and is worth doing for any new doctor.

Ask practical questions too. How quickly can you get a same day sick visit? Who answers messages through the patient portal, and how long do replies take? Are labs drawn on site? Does the practice offer telehealth, and who covers after hours calls? Pay attention to how the front desk treats you on the phone, because you will deal with them often. Be wary of offices that cannot explain their billing or that rush through your history at the first visit. This guide is general consumer information, not medical advice.

faqs.q: How do I check a doctor's license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Search the Georgia Composite Medical Board's online licensee lookup. It shows whether the license is active and lists any public Board orders.

faqs.q: What is the difference between family medicine and internal medicine?
faqs.a: Family medicine doctors typically see patients of all ages, including children. Internal medicine doctors focus on adults.

faqs.q: What should I bring to a first primary care visit?
faqs.a: Bring your insurance card, a photo ID, a list of current medications and past medical records or the contact details of your previous doctor.

movers.heading: Choosing a moving company in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Whether you are moving across town from Windward to downtown Alpharetta or relocating out of state, the first thing to check is who regulates your mover. For moves within Georgia, moving companies must hold a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity from the Georgia Department of Public Safety, which keeps a list of licensed household goods movers and publishes a maximum rate tariff that licensed movers cannot exceed. For moves that cross state lines, the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration oversees movers, and you can search a company by name or USDOT number on its Protect Your Move site.

Get written estimates from more than one company, ideally after an in person or video walkthrough. Federal guidance lists red flags that apply to any move: a quote given sight unseen, no written estimate, a company that says it will set the price after loading, demands for cash or a large deposit, and a website with no local address or registration information. For interstate moves, your mover should give you the federal booklet Your Rights and Responsibilities When You Move before the move.

On moving day, compare your inventory with the mover's and note any damage before you sign at delivery. Standard coverage is limited, so ask about added protection. For an in state move, Georgia requires a written claim to the mover within 90 days, and the Department of Public Safety may help if it is not resolved. Summer and the end of each month book up quickly across North Fulton, so reserve early.

faqs.q: Do movers need a license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Yes. Movers handling household goods within Georgia must hold a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity from the Georgia Department of Public Safety, which publishes a list of licensed movers.

faqs.q: How do I check an interstate moving company?
faqs.a: Use the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration's Protect Your Move site to search a mover or broker by name, USDOT number or MC number and see its complaint history.

faqs.q: How long do I have to file a damage claim on a Georgia move?
faqs.a: For a move within Georgia, submit a written claim to the mover within 90 days. Interstate moves follow federal rules, which allow up to nine months after delivery.

house-cleaning.heading: Hiring a house cleaning service in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: House cleaning in Alpharetta usually comes in two forms: an independent cleaner who works on their own, or a company that sends a crew. Independent cleaners often offer more consistency because the same person comes every visit, while companies can cover sick days and larger homes. Decide what you want before calling around. A recurring weekly or biweekly clean, a one time deep clean, a move out clean and post construction cleanup are different jobs, and a clear checklist helps you compare quotes fairly.

Ask every service whether it carries liability insurance and, for companies, whether workers are covered if they are injured in your home. Ask whether cleaners are employees or contractors, whether background checks are done, and who will actually show up. Find out what supplies they bring, whether they will use your products if you have pets, allergies or delicate surfaces, and how they handle keys, garage codes and alarm systems. A walkthrough before the first visit is a good sign.

Get the scope, schedule and cancellation policy in writing, along with what happens if something is damaged or a room is missed. Red flags include a service that will not put anything in writing, asks for large payments up front, or sends a different crew every time without notice. Spring cleaning, the weeks before Thanksgiving and the busy summer moving season in North Fulton fill calendars quickly, so book a deep clean or move out clean several weeks ahead.

faqs.q: Should a house cleaner be insured?
faqs.a: Yes, ask for proof of liability insurance before the first visit. It protects you if something in your home is damaged during cleaning.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a regular clean and a deep clean?
faqs.a: A regular clean maintains surfaces, floors, kitchens and bathrooms. A deep clean adds detailed work such as baseboards, inside appliances and built up grime, and usually takes much longer.

faqs.q: Should I tip my house cleaner?
faqs.a: Tipping is common but optional. Many people tip for deep cleans, at the holidays, or when a cleaner goes beyond the usual checklist.

painters.heading: Hiring a house painter in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Painting looks simple, but most of the result comes from prep work: scraping, sanding, caulking, patching and protecting floors and trim. When you compare painters in Alpharetta, ask each one to describe their prep steps, which paint line and sheen they plan to use, how many coats are included, and whether the crew is their own employees or subcontractors. Get the same detailed scope from every bidder so the quotes are truly comparable.

Georgia's state consumer protection office notes that painters are among the specialty trades exempt from the state's residential and general contractor license, so a painter will not have a state license to check. That makes other proof more important. Ask for a certificate of liability insurance, confirm the business holds any required city or county business license, and call references for jobs similar to yours. If your home was built before 1978, ask how the crew handles possible lead paint during sanding and removal.

The state's consumer office lists warning signs that apply here: door to door solicitation, cash only payment, pressure for an immediate decision, an unusually long guarantee, and requests to pay for the entire job up front. Put start and finish dates, colors, warranty terms and a staged payment schedule in a written contract. Exterior work in North Fulton is easiest in spring and fall, when temperatures and humidity suit most paints, so good crews book those months early. If you live in an HOA community, get color approval before work begins.

faqs.q: Do painters need a license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Painters are exempt from Georgia's state residential and general contractor license, according to Georgia's state consumer protection office. Most are still subject to city or county business licensing, so ask for that and proof of insurance.

faqs.q: How should I pay a painting contractor?
faqs.a: Avoid paying for the whole job up front. Tie payments to completed stages of the work and keep a final payment until you have inspected the finished job.

faqs.q: What is the best time of year to paint a house exterior?
faqs.a: Spring and fall are usually the easiest seasons in the Atlanta area because moderate temperatures and lower humidity help paint cure. Always follow the paint maker's temperature guidance.

garage-door.heading: Choosing a garage door company in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Garage doors are heavy, and the springs that lift them are under serious tension, so most repairs beyond a simple remote or sensor adjustment are best left to a trained technician. When you call a company in Alpharetta, describe the symptoms clearly: a door that will not open, a loud bang from a broken spring, a door that reverses, or cables that have come loose. A good company will explain the likely cause, give a written estimate before starting, and tell you whether the parts are standard or brand specific.

Ask whether the company has a physical local address, carries liability insurance and holds any city or county business license required where it operates. Georgia's consumer protection office notes that most contractors are subject to local licensing even when a trade is not state licensed. Ask about the warranty on parts and labor separately, and whether replacement springs are rated for more cycles than the originals. If you are replacing the whole door, ask about insulation, wind rating and HOA approval before ordering.

Watch for the warning signs Georgia's consumer office lists for home repair: pressure to decide immediately, a demand for full payment up front, cash only terms, and offers to use leftover materials from another job. Be cautious with online ads that show no local address and quote a low service call that grows once the technician arrives. Broken springs often fail on cold mornings, so knowing a reliable company before you need one can save a stressful wait.

faqs.q: Can I replace a garage door spring myself?
faqs.a: Springs store a lot of tension and can cause serious injury if handled incorrectly. Most homeowners are safer hiring a trained technician for spring and cable work.

faqs.q: Why does my garage door reverse before it closes?
faqs.a: A common cause is misaligned or blocked safety sensors near the bottom of the track. If cleaning and realigning them does not help, call a technician.

faqs.q: What should a garage door estimate include?
faqs.a: It should list parts, labor, any trip charge and warranty terms in writing before work begins.

handymen.heading: Hiring a handyman in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: A good handyman is ideal for the punch list that piles up in any house: patching drywall, hanging doors, fixing trim, mounting TVs, replacing fixtures and small carpentry jobs. Before you call, write down every task with photos so you can get a clear quote and avoid repeat trip charges. Ask whether the handyman bills by the hour or by the job, who buys materials, and whether they can finish everything in one visit or need to come back.

Georgia's state consumer protection office notes that repair handymen are generally exempt from the state's residential and general contractor license, but utility trades are different. Plumbing, electrical and air conditioning work is regulated by the Georgia Construction Industry Licensing Board, so a handyman should not be taking on that work unless properly licensed. Larger projects that go beyond repairs may also require a licensed contractor and building permits. Ask for proof of liability insurance and any city or county business license, and be wary if someone asks you to pull the permits yourself.

The state lists other red flags worth knowing: door to door solicitation, cash only payment, pressure to decide on the spot, and requests to pay for the whole job before work starts. Get the task list, completion date and price in writing, and pay in stages for anything larger than a short visit. Reliable handymen in North Fulton often book out a few weeks, especially before the holidays and in spring, so reach out early if you are preparing to sell or host guests.

faqs.q: Does a handyman need a license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Georgia's consumer protection office says repair handymen are generally exempt from the state residential contractor license. Plumbing, electrical and HVAC work requires a license from the Georgia Construction Industry Licensing Board.

faqs.q: Should I pull permits for my handyman?
faqs.a: Georgia's consumer office lists a contractor asking you to get the required permits as a warning sign. The person doing the work should know what permits are needed.

faqs.q: How do I get an accurate handyman quote?
faqs.a: Send a written list of every task with photos and measurements. Ask whether the quote is hourly or fixed and whether materials are included.

auto-body.heading: Choosing an auto body shop in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: After a fender bender on GA 400 or in a busy parking lot, the body shop you pick determines how well your car is put back together. Georgia uses a fault based system: the at fault driver's liability insurance pays for damage to others, and the state's Office of Commissioner of Insurance notes you can also file under your own collision coverage even when someone else caused the crash. Ask your agent which route makes more sense for your situation before you choose a shop.

You do not have to use the shop your insurer suggests. Georgia law says an insurer may not require you to use a particular repair facility to settle a claim if you can get the work done at the same cost elsewhere, and it may not suggest that using or avoiding a shop could lead to nonpayment. Get a written estimate, ask whether the shop follows the manufacturer's repair procedures, and find out whether it plans to use original equipment, aftermarket or used parts.

Ask about the shop's warranty on paint and workmanship, how it handles supplemental damage found after teardown, and whether it can recalibrate cameras and sensors that newer cars rely on. Request photos during the repair and a final invoice listing parts and labor. Red flags include pressure to sign a direction to pay before you have seen an estimate, vague answers about parts, and reluctance to let you inspect the car before pickup. Report hit and run damage to police promptly, since your insurer may ask for the report.

faqs.q: Can my insurance company make me use their body shop in Georgia?
faqs.a: No. Georgia law says an insurer may not require you to use a particular repair facility to settle a claim if you can get the repairs at the same cost elsewhere.

faqs.q: Is Georgia an at fault state for car accidents?
faqs.a: Yes. The at fault driver's liability coverage pays for others' damages, and you may also file under your own collision coverage if you carry it.

faqs.q: What parts will be used on my car?
faqs.a: Ask the shop and your insurer whether the estimate calls for original equipment, aftermarket or used parts. Get the answer in writing.

insurance-agents.heading: Choosing an insurance agent in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Insurance agents in Alpharetta generally fall into two groups. Captive agents represent one company, while independent agents can quote several insurers for the same coverage. Neither is automatically better. A captive agent may know one company's products deeply, while an independent agent can shop your home and auto policies when rates change. Ask each agent which companies they represent, how they are paid, and who you will call when you have a claim.

Georgia requires all insurance agents, brokers and adjusters to be licensed by the Office of Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire, and agent licenses are renewed every year. The Commissioner's office offers a free online license lookup, so you can confirm an agent, agency or insurance company is licensed in Georgia before you sign anything. For auto coverage, Georgia law sets minimum liability limits, but many drivers choose higher limits along with uninsured motorist, collision and comprehensive coverage, so ask the agent to explain each piece.

A good agent reviews your full picture, including homes, cars, teen drivers and any business activity, and explains deductibles in plain terms. Ask about discounts the Commissioner's office lists, such as multiple vehicles, good student, safety and anti theft devices, low mileage and bundling home and auto. Red flags include pressure to sign the same day, reluctance to put quotes in writing, or a policy that costs far less than others without a clear reason. Review your coverage each year at renewal. This is general consumer information, not insurance or financial advice.

faqs.q: How do I check if an insurance agent is licensed in Georgia?
faqs.a: Use the license lookup on the Georgia Office of Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire website. It covers agents, agencies and insurance companies.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a captive and an independent agent?
faqs.a: A captive agent sells policies from one insurer. An independent agent can compare quotes from several insurers.

faqs.q: Is uninsured motorist coverage worth asking about in Georgia?
faqs.a: The Commissioner's office explains that uninsured motorist coverage protects you if a driver without insurance damages your car or injures you. Ask your agent how it fits your policy.

tutoring.heading: Choosing a tutoring center in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Alpharetta families use tutoring for very different reasons: catching up in math, staying ahead in advanced classes, preparing for the SAT or ACT, or building study habits. Be specific about the goal before you compare options. Franchise learning centers often use a set curriculum and assessments, while independent tutors and small centers can tailor sessions to what your student is covering in class. Ask whether tutors work with the same course materials your child's Fulton County school uses and how they align lessons with classroom units.

Ask about tutor qualifications, subject expertise, background checks and how a tutor is matched to your child. Find out whether sessions are one on one or small group, how progress is measured and shared with parents, and what happens if your child does not click with a tutor. Georgia Milestones testing starts in grade 3, and many families look for help ahead of end of grade and end of course tests, so ask whether the center has experience with those standards if that is your concern.

If a center also offers after school pickup or supervision, ask whether it is licensed by Georgia's Department of Early Care and Learning or holds an approved exemption, since state law requires anyone caring for more than two children for pay to be licensed or exempt. Be cautious about long prepaid contracts, guaranteed score increases and pressure to enroll on the first visit. Spots fill quickly in August and before winter exams, so start your search a few weeks ahead.

faqs.q: When should my child start tutoring?
faqs.a: It usually helps to start as soon as a teacher raises a concern or grades begin to slip, rather than right before a big test. Early support gives a tutor time to fix gaps.

faqs.q: Do tutoring centers in Georgia need a child care license?
faqs.a: Georgia requires anyone caring for more than two children for pay to be licensed or exempt, and some instructional programs qualify for exemptions. Ask whether the center holds a DECAL license or an approved exemption.

faqs.q: What grades take Georgia Milestones tests?
faqs.a: Georgia Milestones end of grade tests begin in grade 3 and continue through middle school, with end of course tests in certain high school subjects.

martial-arts.heading: Choosing a martial arts school in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Martial arts schools in Alpharetta teach a wide range of styles, from taekwondo and karate to Brazilian jiu jitsu, Krav Maga and kickboxing. Each feels very different, so start with your goal: fitness, self defense, competition, discipline and confidence for kids, or a lifelong hobby. Visit during a real class rather than just a sales tour, and watch how instructors correct students, how they handle beginners and whether classes are grouped sensibly by age and skill.

Ask about the head instructor's training lineage and how long they have taught, how belts or ranks are earned, and what testing involves. Clarify contract terms before signing. Many schools sell memberships with automatic renewals and separate testing or equipment charges, so get the cancellation policy, freeze options and all extra fees in writing. Be wary of high pressure enrollment on a first visit, promises of black belts on a fixed timeline, or reluctance to let you try a class first.

Safety matters most with contact styles. Ask how sparring is supervised, what protective gear is required, how mats are cleaned, and whether instructors have first aid training. Some schools run after school programs that include pickup from local elementary schools. Georgia law requires programs that care for more than two children for pay to be licensed by the Department of Early Care and Learning or hold an approved exemption, and the state treats classes where supervision is only incidental, such as martial arts lessons, under a separate exemption category. If you rely on pickup and supervision, ask which applies.

faqs.q: What age can kids start martial arts?
