faqs.a: Many schools offer classes starting around age 4 or 5, with programs grouped by age. Ask whether the school has a dedicated class for younger beginners.

faqs.q: Do martial arts after school programs need a license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Programs that care for more than two children for pay must be licensed by DECAL or hold an approved exemption. Ask the school which applies to its after school program.

faqs.q: Should I sign a long martial arts contract?
faqs.a: Try a few classes first and read the cancellation and renewal terms carefully. Get any promises about freezes or refunds in writing.

dance-studios.heading: Choosing a dance studio in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Dance studios in Alpharetta range from recreational schools where kids try ballet, tap and hip hop for fun to competition studios with demanding rehearsal schedules, plus adult programs in ballroom, salsa and fitness dance. Start by deciding how much time your family wants to commit. A recreational class once a week and a competition team that travels most weekends are very different experiences, and many studios offer both tracks.

Watch a class or book a trial before enrolling. Look at how teachers correct technique, whether younger students are taught age appropriate movement, and whether the floors are sprung or cushioned rather than concrete covered in vinyl. Ask about teacher training and experience, class sizes, and how students move between levels. Get a full picture of the season up front, including recital or competition costume fees, required dancewear, rehearsal requirements and any registration charges, so there are no surprises in the spring.

If the studio offers after school pickup or long camp days, ask how children are supervised between classes. Georgia law requires anyone caring for more than two children for pay to be licensed by the Department of Early Care and Learning or hold an approved exemption, and the state has a separate exemption category for classes such as dance lessons where supervision is only incidental. Ask which applies if you rely on the studio for care. Fall enrollment opens in late summer and popular classes fill quickly across North Fulton, so register early.

faqs.q: What age should a child start dance classes?
faqs.a: Many studios offer creative movement or combination classes for preschoolers, with formal technique classes starting around school age. Ask about the studio's youngest class and what it covers.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a recreational and a competition dance studio?
faqs.a: Recreational programs focus on weekly classes and an annual recital. Competition programs add extra rehearsals, travel and choreography fees, and require a bigger time commitment.

faqs.q: Do dance studios need a child care license in Georgia?
faqs.a: Studios that care for more than two children for pay need a DECAL license or an approved exemption, and the state has an exemption category for lessons like dance. Ask the studio which applies to its programs.

hotels.heading: Choosing a hotel in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Where you stay in Alpharetta depends on why you are visiting. The city's tourism office lists hotels clustered around Avalon and Old Milton Parkway, along North Point Parkway, and on Windward Parkway. Business travelers often pick a hotel close to their meetings to avoid crossing GA 400 at rush hour, while leisure visitors may prefer to be within walking distance of Avalon's shops and restaurants or a short ride from downtown Alpharetta.

If you are coming for a concert at Ameris Bank Amphitheatre, a tournament or a wedding, book early. Big event weekends can fill rooms across the area, and group blocks usually have a cutoff date. Check whether the hotel offers a shuttle, since some Alpharetta properties do, and confirm parking arrangements, especially near Avalon. Alpharetta's tourism office notes the city is about 30 minutes from Atlanta, but traffic on GA 400 can stretch that considerably, so plan airport trips with extra time.

Before booking, compare the total stay rather than the nightly rate alone, including taxes, resort or parking fees and pet fees. Read the cancellation policy closely, especially on prepaid rates booked through third party sites, which can be harder to change. Ask whether breakfast is included, whether the hotel has meeting space or a pool if you need it, and how far the nearest restaurants are on foot. Booking directly with the hotel can make special requests and changes easier.

faqs.q: What areas of Alpharetta have hotels?
faqs.a: Alpharetta's tourism office lists hotels around Avalon and Old Milton Parkway, along North Point Parkway and on Windward Parkway. Choose based on whether you need to be near offices, shopping or event venues.

faqs.q: How far is Alpharetta from Atlanta?
faqs.a: Alpharetta's tourism office describes it as about 30 minutes from Atlanta. Rush hour traffic on GA 400 can add significant time.

faqs.q: Are there pet friendly hotels in Alpharetta?
faqs.a: Yes, several Alpharetta hotels accept pets. Confirm the pet policy, weight limits and any fees when you book.

dog-grooming.heading: Choosing a dog groomer or boarding facility in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Grooming and boarding both mean handing your dog to someone else for hours or days, so trust matters more than convenience. In Georgia, kennel operators, a category the Georgia Department of Agriculture says includes groomers, trainers and boarders, are licensed and inspected by the department's companion animal program. The department offers a free online license search, so check that a groomer or boarding facility appears before your first visit, and use its complaint process if you see problems.

Expect a good facility to ask for proof of vaccinations. Fulton County requires dogs four months and older to be vaccinated against rabies and to carry a county license that runs on the same term as the vaccine, so keep your certificate handy. Ask what other vaccines are required for boarding or daycare, how dogs are grouped during play, how often staff check on boarded dogs overnight, and which veterinarian they call in an emergency. Tour the space, notice the smell and noise level, and ask whether dogs are ever left unattended in dryers or crates.

For grooming, ask how the groomer handles anxious or senior dogs, whether they use cage dryers or hand drying, and how long your dog will be there. Share any health issues, skin sensitivities or behavior concerns at drop off. Red flags include refusing to let you see where dogs are kept, vague answers about supervision, or no vaccination requirements at all. Boarding spots around Alpharetta fill up quickly for Thanksgiving, winter holidays, spring break and summer travel, so reserve well in advance.

faqs.q: Do dog groomers need a license in Georgia?
faqs.a: The Georgia Department of Agriculture licenses kennel operators, which it says includes groomers, trainers and boarders. You can check a business with the department's online license search.

faqs.q: Does Fulton County require a dog license?
faqs.a: Yes. Fulton County requires dogs four months and older to be vaccinated against rabies and licensed, with the license term matching the rabies vaccine.

faqs.q: What vaccines do boarding facilities require?
faqs.a: Rabies is required by law, and many facilities also ask for other vaccines. Ask the facility for its full list before booking.

senior-living.heading: Choosing a senior living community in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Senior living options around Alpharetta include independent living communities, assisted living communities, smaller personal care homes and memory care. Start with an honest look at the help your loved one needs now and may need in a few years, such as medication reminders, bathing, dressing or supervision for memory loss, because that determines which setting fits. Visit more than once, including at a meal, and talk with residents and families if you can.

Georgia's Department of Community Health, through its Healthcare Facility Regulation Division, licenses personal care homes and assisted living communities. Under state rules, an assisted living community is a personal care home serving 25 or more residents that is licensed to provide assisted living care. The department conducts unannounced inspections roughly every 11 to 15 months and investigates complaints, so ask the community for its license and recent inspection results. Georgia's consumer protection office warns that an unlicensed home advertising for residents violates the Fair Business Practices Act.

Ask about staffing levels on each shift, staff training, how care needs are reassessed, and what happens if needs grow beyond what the community can provide. Get every fee and what triggers a change in writing, and read the residency agreement before signing. Red flags include reluctance to share inspection results, high staff turnover and pressure to sign before you have toured. Georgia's Long Term Care Ombudsman Program advocates for residents of personal care homes and assisted living facilities and can help resolve problems. This is general guidance, not legal or financial advice.

faqs.q: How do I check if an assisted living community is licensed in Georgia?
faqs.a: Personal care homes and assisted living communities are licensed by the Georgia Department of Community Health's Healthcare Facility Regulation Division. Ask the community for its license and recent survey results, or contact the division.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a personal care home and assisted living in Georgia?
faqs.a: Under Georgia rules, an assisted living community is a personal care home with 25 or more residents that is licensed to provide assisted living care. Smaller personal care homes provide housing, meals and personal services.

faqs.q: Who can help if there is a problem at a senior care facility?
faqs.a: Georgia's Long Term Care Ombudsman Program investigates and helps resolve resident complaints. You can also file a complaint with the Department of Community Health.

wedding-venues.heading: Choosing a wedding or event venue in Alpharetta: what to know
paras: Alpharetta and the surrounding North Fulton area offer everything from historic homes and gardens to hotel ballrooms, rustic barns and modern event spaces. Begin with your guest count and the feel you want, then visit venues at the same time of day as your event so you can judge lighting, parking and noise. Ask whether the ceremony and reception can be held in the same place, and what the rain plan is for any outdoor space.

Read the contract closely before you sign. Ask what is included, such as tables, chairs, linens and setup, whether you must use the venue's caterer or an approved vendor list, and whether outside alcohol is allowed and who must serve it. Clarify the deposit and payment schedule, cancellation and postponement terms, the exact hours you have access, and any noise curfew. Find out whether a venue coordinator will be on site during the event and whether liability insurance is required. Popular spring and fall Saturdays book far ahead, so weekday or off season dates can open more options.

Do not forget the marriage license. Georgia marriage licenses are issued by county probate courts. If at least one of you is a Georgia resident, the license can come from any Georgia county, and if neither of you lives in Georgia, it must come from the county where the ceremony will take place. Both partners must be at least 18. Couples who complete a qualifying premarital education program of at least six hours within 12 months before applying are not charged the license fee.

faqs.q: Where do I get a marriage license for a wedding in Alpharetta?
faqs.a: Marriage licenses come from Georgia county probate courts. If one partner lives in Georgia, any county can issue it; if neither does, apply in the county where the ceremony will be held.

faqs.q: Does Georgia have a premarital education discount?
faqs.a: Yes. Couples who present a certificate from a qualifying premarital education program of at least six hours, completed within 12 months, are not assessed the marriage license fee.

faqs.q: How far ahead should I book a wedding venue?
faqs.a: Popular Saturdays in spring and fall often book many months ahead. Tour early and get your date in a signed contract.
